images.title: An eye from two arcs
images.purpose: Show an eye drawn as two compass arcs that meet at two corners X and Y.
images.composition: One large eye in the centre on a white background, with the segment XY drawn faintly through it.
exact_structure: A horizontal grey (#6B7280) segment from point X on the left to point Y on the right, about half the frame wide.
An upper teal (#0072B2) arc that starts at X, bulges upwards and ends at Y.
A lower teal (#0072B2) arc that starts at X, bulges downwards by the same amount and ends at Y, so the shape is symmetrical about XY.
A solid dark circle (the pupil) at the midpoint of XY, inside the eye.
Small dark dots at X and Y with the labels X and Y just outside the eye.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: An eye is two equal arcs that both pass through the corners X and Y.
images.description: Show an eye drawn as two compass arcs that meet at two corners X and Y.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.

image_decisions.why: Students need to see the two arcs meeting at X and Y to ask where their centres are.
